To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sleep, in particular a combination of REM sleep and NREM sleep, contributes to memory consolidation by strengthening memory and by removing weak memory traces.

(1) simulated sleep contributes to learning in the network; (2) simulated sleep can be divided into two types, one of which is associated with forgetting, the other with memory consolidation; and (3) the relationship between simulated sleep and learning can be represented by an inverted U-shaped function, with a peak at an intermediate level of simulated sleep.

1) the effect of sleep on learning depends on the type of sleep, 2) NREM sleep leads to general reinforcement of memory while REM sleep leads to forgetting, 3) the effect of REM sleep on learning is stronger when preceded by NREM sleep, 4) the overall effect of sleep on consolidation depends on the relative amount of NREM and REM sleep.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible contribution of the REM and NREM sleep cycles to memory consolidation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sleep is not necessary for the consolidation of long-term memory, however, it does appear to be necessary for the consolidation and forgetting of some memories.
the relationship between sleep and memory consolidation is not a straightforward one.
the sleep cycle is a necessary, though not a sufficient, condition for effective consolidation of memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an abstract model that is able to simulate the contribution of sleep to the consolidation of memories.
sleep is not just for forgetting but also for remembering.
sleep is a state of memory consolidation and that it is not just a passive process but an active process that involves the reorganization of the memory traces in the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of the sleep process can be modelled using a simple neural network model.
the dynamics of the neural networks during sleep may play a role in the consolidation of memory.
the dynamics of sleep may contribute to the consolidation of memory by allowing the brain to ‘revisit’ memories and by selectively strengthening the memory traces that are more likely to be relevant.
